extracted.intended_audience: IP litigators, in-house counsel, and corporate counsel dealing with antitrust and patent litigation
extracted.subtask_short: antitrust pleading in patent aggregator suits
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for pleading and defending antitrust claims arising from disputes between non-practicing entities (patent trolls) and patent aggregators/members; focuses on what factual detail and legal theories are required to survive a motion to dismiss. Useful for lawyers drafting complaints or motions in related IP/antitrust litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleading specificity for conspiracy claims (Twombly/Iqbal)
rubrics_metrics.description: A plaintiff must allege the necessary specifics of a conspiracy claim — i.e., 'who, did what, to whom (or with whom), where, and when.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General allegations of 'agreements with RPX, joint defense agreements, NPE insurance, common counsel, meetings, phone calls, emails, and discussions' were held insufficient under Bell Atl. Corp. v. Twombly. Complaints must identify concrete facts showing the existence of an agreement and each defendant's role; boilerplate or conclusory descriptions will not survive a motion to dismiss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate definition of the relevant market
rubrics_metrics.description: A complaint must clearly define the relevant product and geographic market for antitrust purposes; vague or internally inconsistent market definitions are inadequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The court criticized pleading that described the market as broadly as 'licenses' and as narrowly as 'Cascades' patents,' calling such oscillation 'subterfuge.' Plaintiffs should plead a coherent, well-defined market and factual support for that market definition to show market power or anticompetitive effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plead facts supporting a group boycott theory (vs. individual disputes)
rubrics_metrics.description: To state a group boycott claim, plaintiffs must plead how the alleged harm resulted from a concerted group boycott rather than from individual business disputes or tactical negotiation conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The court rejected allegations that could be explained as 'individual business disputes.' Plaintiffs should plead facts showing coordinated refusal to deal or collective concerted action causing anticompetitive effects, not merely parallel or independent conduct arising from licensing negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic plausibility / plausibility of anticompetitive theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations must make economic sense and be plausibly explained; courts will not presume economic rationality where facts suggest a tactical ploy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The court stated: 'Without clarification and specificity, the Court will not presume economic rationality where the circumstances giving rise to the lawsuit plausibly suggest nothing more than a tactical ploy to regain economic leverage.' Complaints should include facts explaining why the defendants would economically benefit from the alleged anticompetitive scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory counterclaim and transactional relatedness
rubrics_metrics.description: Antitrust claims may be subject to dismissal if they should have been raised as compulsory counterclaims in earlier litigation, which requires that the claims 'arise out of the same transaction or occurrence.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defendants argued the antitrust complaint should have been asserted in Illinois as a compulsory counterclaim; the court found the suits did not 'arise out of the same transaction or occurrence' here. Parties should evaluate whether antitrust claims are procedurally barred as compulsory counterclaims based on transactional relatedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noerr-Pennington doctrine as a potential defense
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerted activity undertaken in response to litigation may be protected by the Noerr-Pennington doctrine, potentially immunizing defendants from antitrust liability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The court noted the defendants' concerted activity may have been undertaken in response to Illinois infringement litigation and thus might be Noerr-Pennington protected; however, the court could not resolve that defense on the face of the pleadings. Determination of Noerr protection may require factual development beyond the complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to plead a factual nexus between conduct and anticompetitive harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Plaintiffs must plead specific facts linking defendants' concerted conduct to actual anticompetitive harm rather than relying on conclusory assertions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The opinion demonstrates that vague, general allegations of collusion or concerted activity are insufficient. Plaintiffs should allege who did what, the mechanism of the alleged boycott or exclusionary conduct, the relevant market, and factual allegations showing how that conduct produced anticompetitive effects.
